title: Astronomers Spot a Strange Atmospheric Wave Above Saturn’s South Pole - Nautilus
gist: Astronomers have identified a new decagon-shaped (10-sided) atmospheric wind pattern spanning Saturn's south pole that appears to have formed between 2023 and 2025, echoing the long-stable hexagonal pattern known at the planet's north pole since 1980.

insights.claim: Saturn's north pole has hosted a stable hexagonal wind pattern for roughly 40 years, first spotted by the Voyager probes in 1980-1981, illustrating that Saturn's atmospheric structures can persist far longer than any weather pattern on Earth.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Establishes a multi-decade baseline of atmospheric stability on Saturn, the comparison point against which the new south-pole feature's persistence will be judged.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning "To take as one example"

insights.claim: A newly identified decagon-shaped (10-sided) wind pattern has formed over Saturn's south pole sometime between 2023 and 2025, covering a huge area, and researchers suggest it could persist for decades given the precedent set by the north pole's hexagon.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: A newly forming, potentially multi-decade planetary weather feature gives astronomers a fresh natural experiment to test atmospheric dynamics models on gas giants.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning "Now, though, the planet’s south pole"
